obligations.condition: Password sign-in of the target before the disable; tokens name the target and serve a derived lookup.
Password sign-in of the control before the disable.

Privileged accounts:update replacing the disabled target's password. Accepted and refused are both valid; if accepted, the update must be visible through privileged lookup with the account still disabled, and whether tokens were returned is recorded.
If the update returned an ID token, accounts:lookup with it; executed exactly when tokens were returned.
If the update returned a refresh token, it is redeemed; executed exactly when tokens were returned.
Privileged accounts:update setting the disabled target's photoUrl; accepted and refused are both valid; if accepted, the readback shows the value with the account still disabled.
The disabled target's own password sign-in with the replaced password; accepted and refused are both valid.
The control signs in while the target is disabled.
The target's password sign-in with the replaced password after re-enablement; accepted and refused are both valid.
The control signs in after the target is re-enabled.

limitations: URLs were read during design; no new frozen full-body source snapshot or completed page-review claim is made by this mapping.

The sources document that a privileged update may change a disabled user's fields; they do not state whether tokens are returned for a disabled account. The observation, not the sources, answers that for the recorded conditions.
Two update fields (password, photoUrl), no tenant, a single run; other fields, self-service updates by a disabled user and SDK behavior are outside this mapping.
No execution approval, independent signature verification, SDK or Rules claim follows from this mapping.
